Negative binomial regression

Source: R/nbreg.R
nbreg.Rd

Fits a negative binomial (NB2) regression model with log link, \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta\). The coefficients \(\beta\) are estimated by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) with \(\theta\) held fixed, alternated with Newton-Raphson updates of \(\log\theta\) with \(\beta\) held fixed, until the log-likelihood stops changing. No general-purpose numerical maximizer is used.

Usage

nbreg(formula, data, offset, control = nbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A model formula, response ~ covariates. Offsets may be given in the formula with offset().

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

An optional offset vector (e.g. log exposure), evaluated in data. Added to any offset() terms in the formula.

control

A list of settings from nbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "nbreg", a list with components

coefficients

estimated regression coefficients \(\hat\beta\)

vcov

variance-covariance matrix of \(\hat\beta\)

theta, SE.theta

estimated dispersion parameter and its standard error

loglik

maximized log-likelihood

iter, converged

number of outer iterations and whether the log-likelihood converged

fitted.values, linear.predictors

\(\hat\mu_i\) and \(\hat\eta_i\)

y, offset, nobs, df.residual

response, offset, number of observations, and residual degrees of freedom

call, terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, control

information used to print the fit and to predict for new data

Details

The algorithm starts from a Poisson fit (IRLS with \(\theta = \infty\)) and the moment estimate \(\theta_0 = n / \sum_i (y_i/\mu_i - 1)^2\). Standard errors of \(\hat\beta\) come from \((X^\top \hat W X)^{-1}\), treating \(\theta\) as known, and the standard error of \(\hat\theta\) is \(\{-H(\hat\theta)\}^{-1/2}\), where \(H\) is the second derivative of the log-likelihood in \(\theta\).

See also

nbreg_control(), zinbreg()

Examples

# Simulated data with known beta = (0.5, 0.3) and theta = 2
set.seed(1)
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
y <- rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.3 * x))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = data.frame(x, y))
fit$coefficients
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4154160   0.3302077 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.70792

# Publication counts of biochemistry PhD students
if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit2 <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
  cbind(estimate = fit2$coefficients, se = sqrt(diag(fit2$vcov)))
}
#>                estimate          se
#> (Intercept)  0.25614402 0.137347701
#> femWomen    -0.21641842 0.072636088
#> marMarried   0.15048945 0.082096542
#> kid5        -0.17641524 0.052813297
#> phd          0.01527116 0.035872991
#> ment         0.02908234 0.003214319
